elements.quote: DESIGN AND SETTING: Rapid systematic review conducted in the medical school of the Federal University of São Paulo (SP), Brazil.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly labels the study as a 'Rapid systematic review.'

elements.quote: OBJECTIVE: To assess whether patients undergoing pharmacological treatment for IMID present higher risk of worse outcomes when diagnosed with COVID-19.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a clear objective/review question.

elements.quote: METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, EMBASE, LILACS, SCOPUS, Web of Science, L·OVE, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO-ICTRP for studies evaluating patients diagnosed with COVID-19 who were undergoing pharmacological treatment for IMID.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main inclusion population (patients with COVID-19 undergoing pharmacological treatment for IMID) but does not state any explicit exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, EMBASE, LILACS, SCOPUS, Web of Science, L·OVE, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO-ICTRP for studies evaluating patients diagnosed with COVID-19 who were undergoing pharmacological treatment for IMID.
elements.reason: The abstract lists the information sources searched but does not report when the searches were last conducted (no search date given in the abstract).

elements.quote: Two authors selected studies, extracted data and assessed risk of bias and certainty of evidence, following the Cochrane recommendations.
elements.reason: The abstract states that risk of bias was assessed by two authors following Cochrane recommendations, which describes the method used to assess risk of bias.

elements.quote: RESULTS: We identified 1,498 references, from which one cohort study was included. This compared patients with and without rheumatic diseases (RD) who all had been diagnosed with COVID-19. Those with RD seemed to have higher chances of hospitalization and mortality, but no statistical difference was detected between the groups: hospitalization: odds ratio (OR) 1.17; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.6 to 2.29; mortality rate: OR 1.53; 95% CI 0.33 to 7.11 (very low certainty of evidence). Patients with RD were three times more likely to require admission to intensive care units (ICUs), with invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), than those without RD: OR 3.72; 95% CI 1.35 to 10.26 (for both outcomes; very low certainty of evidence).
elements.reason: The abstract reports numerical results (ORs and CIs) but does not explicitly describe the methods used for presenting or synthesizing results (e.g., meta-analysis methods or narrative synthesis approach).

elements.quote: RESULTS: We identified 1,498 references, from which one cohort study was included.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of references identified and that one cohort study was included, but it does not report the total number of participants or detailed study characteristics in the abstract.

elements.quote: Those with RD seemed to have higher chances of hospitalization and mortality, but no statistical difference was detected between the groups: hospitalization: odds ratio (OR) 1.17; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.6 to 2.29; mortality rate: OR 1.53; 95% CI 0.33 to 7.11 ... Patients with RD were three times more likely to require admission to intensive care units (ICUs), with invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), than those without RD: OR 3.72; 95% CI 1.35 to 10.26 (for both outcomes; very low certainty of evidence).
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes (hospitalization, mortality, ICU admission/IMV) including effect estimates and confidence intervals.

elements.quote: RESULTS: We identified 1,498 references, from which one cohort study was included.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted (only one cohort study was included), so reporting a summary estimate from meta-analysis is not applicable.

elements.quote: Those with RD seemed to have higher chances of hospitalization and mortality... Patients with RD were three times more likely to require admission to intensive care units (ICUs), with invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), than those without RD: OR 3.72; 95% CI 1.35 to 10.26 (for both outcomes; very low certainty of evidence).
elements.reason: When comparing groups (with RD vs without RD) the abstract indicates the direction of effect (higher risk for patients with RD) and the outcomes favored the non-RD group.

elements.quote: mortality rate: OR 1.53; 95% CI 0.33 to 7.11 (very low certainty of evidence) ... OR 3.72; 95% CI 1.35 to 10.26 (for both outcomes; very low certainty of evidence).
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the certainty of evidence is 'very low', which summarizes an important limitation of the included evidence.

elements.quote: CONCLUSION: Patients undergoing pharmacological treatment for IMID seem to present higher chances of requiring admission to ICUs, with IMV. Additional high-quality studies are needed to analyze the effects of different treatments for IMID.

No retrieved text explicitly describes the current state of knowledge or important uncertainties about the topic; no introduction or background text was provided in the evidence set.
No retrieved text explains the importance or need for conducting the review; the provided chunks cover methods, search results, and appraisal but do not state the review's rationale or importance.

elements.quote: We read 20 full-text articles to assess the possibility of inclusion. We excluded 4 case series and 15 case-report studies, 9-27 because these study designs were not appropriate for assessing prognosis questions.
elements.reason: The review is focused on prognosis/questions about patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases and COVID-19 (not a review of intervention effects); the text explicitly notes prognosis questions, so the requirement to describe intervention mechanisms does not apply.

elements.quote: We read 20 full-text articles to assess the possibility of inclusion. We excluded 4 case series and 15 case-report studies, 9-27 because these study designs were not appropriate for assessing prognosis questions.
elements.reason: The review addresses prognosis/observational questions rather than complex interventions or delivery contexts; therefore a logic model for intervention components is not applicable.

elements.quote: To assess whether patients undergoing pharmacological treatment for IMID are at higher risk of worse outcomes when diagnosed with COVID-19.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the review objective as assessing whether patients receiving pharmacological treatment for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMID) are at higher risk of worse outcomes with COVID-19.

No evidence in the provided text specifies planned comparisons using PICO or an equivalent framework; the retrieved sections do not present explicit PICO elements or planned intervention/comparator/outcome comparisons.

elements.quote: We planned to include cohort and case-control studies, and if no better evidence were available, we planned to also consider case series and electronic health records for inclusion. Two review authors selected the studies for inclusion, extracted data from these studies and assessed the risk of bias in these studies and the certainty of evidence for the outcomes. We planned to assess the possibility of pooling the results from the studies included, into meta-analyses when at least two studies were sufficiently homogeneous in terms of design, participants and outcome measurements. If insufficient information or heterogeneous studies were found, we planned to summarize the results only in a qualitative synthesis.
elements.reason: Study designs eligible are specified (cohort, case-control, possibly case series and EHR). However settings and follow-up requirements are not described, so the description of all study characteristics is incomplete.

elements.quote: We conducted a systematic search of the literature on July 5, 2020, in the following databases: ... Studies published in any language since November 2019 were considered for inclusion. The search strategies for each database are presented in Appendix 1. The protocol for this systematic review was registered on the PROSPERO 'International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews' platform (CRD42020179863).
elements.reason: The eligibility period (since November 2019) and language ('any language') are explicitly stated; searches included published, ongoing and unpublished studies (trial registries), addressing publication/report status.
No information was found distinguishing exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.
No explicit specification of the groups used in each synthesis or linkage of those groups to the comparisons defined in the review objectives was found in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: We read 20 full-text articles to assess the possibility of inclusion. We excluded 4 case series and 15 case-report studies, 9-27 because these study designs were not appropriate for assessing prognosis questions.
elements.reason: A rationale is provided for excluding specific study designs (case series and case reports) — they were considered not appropriate for assessing prognosis questions.

elements.quote: We conducted a systematic search of the literature on July 5, 2020, in the following databases: Medline via PubMed, Embase via Elsevier, Cochrane Library - Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), BVS Regional Portal (LILACS), Scopus and Web of Science using relevant descriptors and synonyms, with adaptation of the search to the specifications of each database, to identify published, ongoing and unpublished studies.
